title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired couple lost nearly $800,000 to a cryptocurrency scam that exploited trust and false information displays. A stranger contacted them via WhatsApp and directed them to a trading app, which was real, but scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that showed false account balances and fabricated transaction records. The victim saw what appeared to be legitimate returns on his screen and gradually increased his investments, only discovering the fraud when a large withdrawal was denied.

This is a failure of visual authentication at the user interface. The scammers used an AI-generated website to create a false intermediary layer between the real trading app and what the victim saw, making fraudulent account information indistinguishable from truth. A human verification step, such as requiring direct confirmation with the trading platform through official channels before large withdrawals, could have caught the discrepancy. It is not established whether the trading app itself had security lapses that enabled the scammers to conduct this attack, or what platform hosted the fake website.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer encouraged Jerry Dunaway to invest using a mobile trading app, gradually building trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts. Over time, Jerry increased his investments, believing he was seeing legitimate returns on his account. The scheme unraveled when he attempted a larger withdrawal and was denied access to his funds.

Police determined that while the trading app was real, scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that displayed false account information to manipulate what Jerry saw on his screen. The couple, now financially devastated, is speaking publicly to warn others about sophisticated scam tactics. Gwinnett County police are investigating, though authorities note that victims in these cases rarely recover their lost funds. Their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help the couple cover daily expenses.
